newsitem.title: USA: Aon pursuing legal action to recoup charge.
newsitem.headline: Aon pursuing legal action to recoup charge.

text.p: Aon Corp, which took a $27 million charge in the second quarter due to losses it discovered in the portfolio of a recently acquired business, said Tuesday it is pursuing legal options to try to recover that cost.

"We are now pursuing legal issues," Aon Chairman Patrick Ryan told a conference call, but declined to say what specific steps Aon may take to recoup the charge that amounted to $0.10 a share after tax.

Earlier, Aon said it took the charge to recognize investment losses incurred at Alexander & Alexander Services Inc (A&A) before Aon bought that business for about $1.23 billion in the first quarter of 1997.
Aon said the losses related to highly volatile securities such as inverse floater tranches of collateralized mortgage obligations, a mortgage derivative product.
"This activity was hidden from the management of A&A. Our people did quite a good job of finding it through internal audit," Ryan said.
Ryan said Aon's financial recourse could be limited by the fact it bought A&A from the public. In January, Aon completed a $17.50 a share tender offer for A&A.

"The biggest issue frankly from our point of view is we know we got it all," Ryan said. "We're not discounting the value of the $27 million (charge). We'll try to recover it from wherever we have (recourse)...But we know we've got it."
Ryan said he did not believe that Aon was at risk for fines because of the securities discovered in A&A's portfolio.
Insurance companies face some limitations on the kinds of investments they can hold for fiduciary funds.
Aon said it has contacted law enforcement officials regarding the discovery of the securities in A&A's portfolio. A spokesman declined to give further details.

Separately, Aon, which has made several acquisitions, is on track to realize $240 million to $250 million in annual savings beginning in 1998. About $35 million of those savings have been realized in the first half of 1997.
"We feel quite good about the progress that we have made," he said.
He added that the bulk of the savings will be realized in the third and fourth quarters of 1997.
In the second quarter, Aon completed the purchase of the Minet Group from St. Paul Cos Inc and on July 3 closed its tender offer for the Canadian brokerage firm, Sodarcan Inc.
"Both Minet and Sodarcan are excellent strategic fits, as our momentum in the insurance brokerage and consulting business continues to build," Ryan said in a statement.
